identity.title: AstaBench: Rigorous Benchmarking of AI Agents with a Scientific Research Suite

problem.claim: How to rigorously benchmark AI agents’ ability to perform scientific research.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks lack reproducible tools, confounder control, standardized prototyping interfaces, holistic real-world measures, and comprehensive baselines.

contributions.claim: AstaBench contains 2,400+ problems across the scientific discovery process and multiple domains, including problems inspired by deployed-agent user requests.
A scientific research environment provides production-grade search tools intended to support controlled, reproducible evaluation and better confounder accounting.
The authors provide nine science-optimized classes of Asta agents and numerous baselines.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their environment as the first scientific research environment with production-grade search tools for controlled, reproducible evaluation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating 57 agents across 22 agent classes and finding that, despite meaningful progress on individual aspects, AI remains far from solving science research assistance.

narrative_sequence.summary: AI agents are being developed for literature review, experiment replication, data analysis, and proposing research directions.
The authors argue that rigorous evaluation is critical, while identifying five shortcomings in existing benchmarks.
They define benchmarking principles and tooling, then introduce AstaBench as a broad scientific-research suite.
The suite adds production-grade search tools plus science-optimized agent classes and baselines.
Evaluation across 57 agents and 22 classes indicates substantial remaining difficulty in science research assistance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects benchmark design to reproducible tools, confounder accounting, standardized interfaces, holistic tasks, and comprehensive baselines.

lessons.interpretation: A benchmark claim becomes more informative when the suite specifies both evaluation infrastructure and coverage of realistic task demands.
lessons.application: When introducing a benchmark, map each identified evaluation failure to a concrete design element and report the resulting task, tool, and baseline coverage.
lessons.exception: This mapping may be unsuitable when the research question intentionally isolates a single capability or prohibits product-level and tool-mediated evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not report task-level scores, statistical analyses, cost or tool-access controls, or details of reproducibility procedures.
The meaning of “far from solving” and the criteria for “meaningful progress” are not quantified.
The abstract does not establish that the stated first-of-its-kind distinction is independently verified.
